title: This Startup Is Trying to Bring Back Twitter
paragraphs: After Elon Musk bought Twitter and changed its name to X, many people missed the old blue bird. Now, a startup is trying to bring Twitter back.
Musk bought Twitter for $44 billion in October 2022. In July 2023, he changed the name of the platform to X, and the famous blue bird logo was replaced.

A startup from the US state of Virginia, called Operation Bluebird, believes that X gave up its right to the "Twitter" name when it changed its brand. In late August 2026, the company launched a new social network called Twitter.now.

The new platform has no connection to the old Twitter company or to Musk's X. However, it looks and works a lot like the old version of Twitter. For example, users can reply to posts and "retweet" them, and the site uses a blue bird logo.

X does not agree with Operation Bluebird. It says it still owns the Twitter name and logo. X has taken the startup to court in the state of Delaware, and it has asked the court to stop the new platform for now.
Operation Bluebird, on the other hand, argues that X stopped using the names "Twitter" and "tweet," so it should no longer be able to control them.

The court case could be difficult for X, however. At a hearing in April 2026, a judge gave an early opinion suggesting that X may have given up some of its rights connected to the word "tweet" and the bird logo. But no final decision has been made yet.
For now, the future of Twitter.now is uncertain. Whether the platform can keep using the Twitter name will depend on the result of the legal fight with X.
The case shows how valuable a famous brand name can be, even years after a company has stopped using it.
